clue.text: Depots, for sorting, must have county included as part of address

indicators.note: things put out for sorting are about to be rearranged, so the letters get a new order
'included' says one piece is put inside the other, here the county going in

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Co. is the standard abbreviation for county

explanation.surface: Mail depots insist the county appear in an address so letters can be sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcode is the alphanumeric code forming one line of a British mailing address, like a US zip code.

clue.text: To avoid taking risks, has a go with one iron?

blocks.note: to have a go in a game is to play
a means one
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A cautious golfer takes a shot with a single iron club.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf club is a decoy: iron is the metal, by its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To play safe is an idiom for acting cautiously and not running any risk.

clue.text: Long story by another N American Indian chief

blocks.note: a saga is a long story
more means another, additional

explanation.surface: A tribal chief tells yet another long tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagamore is a historical term for a chief among the Algonquian peoples of north-eastern North America.

clue.text: Dreams keep son unsettled

blocks.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
S is the abbreviation for son
a matter not yet decided is up in the air

explanation.surface: A parent's dreams make a son restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun for a fortress tower; 'unsettled' looks like an anagram signal but is a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in the air is an idiom for fanciful, unrealistic hopes or daydreams.

clue.text: Ineffectual man who wears flashy clothes out East

indicators.note: out means removed, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a dude is a dandy, a showy dresser
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A useless show-off parades his loud outfits in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is something that fails to work, and as an adjective it means useless or not effective.

clue.text: American replaces the Parisian in ring in tented area

indicators.note: one item replacing another means a swap of letters inside a word

blocks.note: a ring is a circle
le is French for 'the'
US is the usual abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American takes over from a Frenchman in the ring of a big-top show.
explanation.walkthrough: The French LE at the end of CIRCLE is swapped out for US.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus is a travelling show staged inside a big top, a large tent, so it is literally a tented area.

clue.text: Edited irrelevant bit about explosive Russian tsar

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so the letters are reshaped
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: An editor cut a pointless passage about a volatile Russian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, known as Ivan the Terrible, was the first ruler of Russia to be crowned as tsar.

clue.text: Make sense, mostly, when coming round in a private hospital

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
coming round something means encircling it

blocks.note: an idea clicks when it suddenly makes sense
taken as written

explanation.surface: Things start to make sense for a patient regaining consciousness in a private hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming round' suggests waking up after surgery, but it is the signal for CLIC to go round IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical establishment, and in Britain the word often names a private hospital or specialist centre.

clue.text: Look at article and fume

blocks.note: to see is to look at
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone reads a newspaper article and gets angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' sounds like a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, just as to fume is to show silent rage.

clue.text: Copper not bothered about bit of commotion caused by gig?

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order
only a little bit of the word is used, its opening letter
about means around, so the jumble surrounds the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
first letter of commotion

explanation.surface: An unruffled police officer deals with a disturbance at a music event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bothered' reads as one phrase meaning calm; split it, so 'not' joins the anagram fodder and 'bothered' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a live music performance, and a pop concert is one kind.

clue.text: Scotsman, one good to us

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is declared a good fellow by the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a traditional Scottish male first name, so it can stand as an example of a Scotsman.

clue.text: Write leopard in when anagrammed

indicators.note: the clue states outright that these words are to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to put the word leopard into a jumbled puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is unusually frank; the whole clue reads almost like a setter's note to self.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop someone a line is an idiom for sending them a short letter or message.

clue.text: Tasted plenty in South Dakota

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
ample means plenty

explanation.surface: Someone ate their fill of the local food on a trip to South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food is to try a little of it, so sampled means tried or tasted.

clue.text: The last word from diner - rice cooked about right

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or tampered with, so the letters are mixed
about means surrounding the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A diner has the final say on how the rice is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Dernier cri is French for 'last cry', borrowed into English for the very latest fashion, just like 'the last word'.

clue.text: Freshwater type caught by one in awfully fast bit of Humber

indicators.note: being caught by something means coming straight after it in the cricket scorebook order, so pieces follow on
something done awfully is done badly, so the word that follows is mangled into a new order
one item placed in another sits inside it
only a small bit of the word is used, its opening letter

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written, then rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one
first letter of Humber

explanation.surface: An angler's fish is hooked by someone in a fast-flowing stretch of the Humber estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: C is followed by a jumble of FAST holding I, then H; the Humber is an estuary in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Catfish are a family of whiskered fish, many living in rivers and lakes, so it is one type of freshwater fish.

clue.text: Fire-watcher giving warning to visitor

blocks.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a visitor from elsewhere is a stranger

explanation.surface: Someone on fire duty alerts a newcomer to the danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'to' is part of the wordplay padding before the visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest ranger patrols woodland and keeps lookout for wildfires, so watching for fire is part of the job.

clue.text: Vessel crossing river shows flag

indicators.note: a boat crossing a stretch of water spans it, so it goes around that piece

blocks.note: a steamer is a steamship
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A ship crossing the river flies its colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant or flag flown from a mast.

clue.text: Others infirm, along with me, here?

definitions.text: Others infirm, along with me, here?

indicators.note: infirm means weak and shaky, so the letters are unsteady and fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person wonders where the frail and they themselves will end up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a place where the infirm and the speaker might live.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest home is a residential home for elderly or infirm people needing care.

clue.text: Happy and healthy, trendy and feel fit? Ten, possibly!

indicators.note: possibly suggests the words could be arranged another way

blocks.note: in means fashionable
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stylish who feels fit and gets ten out of ten for health.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettle means condition, and being in fine fettle is an idiom for being in good health and spirits.

clue.text: Exactly right, boy about cannabis

indicators.note: about means around, so the boy wraps the next piece

blocks.note: a son is a boy
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A parent is proved correct about their boy and his drug habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is an informal British expression meaning precisely accurate.

clue.text: Fashionable school for cricket, maybe

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a school of thought or religious group is a sect

explanation.surface: A trendy school that prides itself on playing cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket here is the chirping creature, not the British bat-and-ball sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a jumping insect, so it is one example, signalled by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Greek god with the head of revered cat

indicators.note: a word's head is its leading letter

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
taken as written
first letter of revered

explanation.surface: A Greek deity wearing the head of a sacred cat, as in Egyptian temple art.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, usually a black leopard or jaguar.

clue.text: River round York¿s centre in flood

indicators.note: going round something means wrapping about it
the centre of a word is its middle pair of letters

blocks.note: the Trent is a major English river
middle two letters of York

explanation.surface: A river running past the middle of York during a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a river of the English Midlands; York's middle letters sit after its first T.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing flow of water, as in a flood or deluge.

clue.text: He's inside house delivering a reference book

indicators.note: something inside another is placed within it

blocks.note: Taurus is one of the twelve astrological houses (signs)
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A man at home hands over a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' means a sign of the zodiac, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing words grouped with their synonyms.

clue.text: Bridge, incomplete in town in Belgium

indicators.note: incomplete means unfinished, so the final letter is missing

blocks.note: a span is a bridge, or the stretch it covers

explanation.surface: An unfinished bridge in a Belgian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Spa is a Belgian resort in the Ardennes whose mineral springs gave all health spas their name.

clue.text: Empty-headed girl, one following bishop and doctor round

indicators.note: following means coming after, fixing the order of the pieces

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I is the Roman numeral one
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A foolish young woman trailing after a bishop and a doctor on their rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is not a container signal here; it gives the ring-shaped O at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bimbo is a derogatory slang term for an attractive but supposedly unintelligent young woman.

clue.text: Character in variety

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's inherent temperament
second meaning: a kind or sort, as in things of this sort

explanation.walkthrough: The short clue reads as a phrase about a varied personality, but the words are two separate meanings joined by a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature can mean someone's basic disposition, and also the kind or type of a thing, as in 'problems of that nature'.

clue.text: Having no worries about heartless judge

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is cut out

blocks.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a referee judges a contest

explanation.surface: Someone unbothered by a judge who has no compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: REFEREE has seven letters, so its heart is the fourth, the middle E.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree describes someone free from anxiety or responsibility, relaxed and untroubled.
